_doc: WREN's lines by trigger. Each trigger has lines per memory stage: 0 = fragmented (rendered with glitches), 1 = recovering, 2 = whole. A line is never repeated until the pool for that trigger and stage is used up. {name} = Patch's name, {robot} = a robot name.
wake: ...carrier... is someone... there? Signal at four percent. Hello?
I don't... I don't know who I am. But I can see you. Small. Blue. Rusty. Hello.
hex_clean: ...that patch of ground. It's... brown. Brown is better than gray.
Signal stronger. Did you do that?
...clean... I remember the word. Not what it was for.
Another one. My static has a shape now.
Every hex you clear, I hear a little more. Keep going, {name}.
That ground hasn't seen the sun in a long time. It's blinking.
The grid just ticked. Somewhere a meter I used to watch moved by one.
I'm starting to remember lists. Lists of hexes. Mostly unfinished.
Clean dirt. The Makers would have called that a start. I call it a start, too.
Hex logged. I've started naming them. That one is 'Not Garbage'.
You're good at this. Annoyingly good. The old fleet took breaks.
milestone: ...ten... ten of something. Is ten a lot? It feels like a lot.
Patterns in the noise. You're making them.
Twenty-five hexes. I can see the street from up here now. Mostly.
Fifty. I remembered my own name for a second. It's gone again. It was short.
A hundred hexes. I can see this whole district without squinting. I don't have eyes, but you know what I mean.
perfect: That bale is perfect. Don't tell the others.
Perfect bale. The scale actually purred.
I would frame that one if I had walls.
robot_built: ...another... voice? No. It doesn't talk. It just hums.
...you made a friend. It's very small.
{robot} is online. It looked at you for a full second before it got to work. I saw that.
A new robot. The old fleet used to hum like that, before the quiet.
{robot} reports for duty. Its first log entry is just the word 'can'. Fair.
You're building a crew. The Makers had a word for that. 'Department.' I don't miss it.
part_rare: ...that... glows. That's old. Older than me?
That part is older than most of this city. Treat it nicely.
Vintage stock. Someone kept that safe for a long time.
Legendary parts don't just turn up. Someone buried that on purpose.
That casing has a serial range I haven't seen since the Cradle was built.
upgrade: New parts. You squeak in a slightly different key now.
Upgrade installed. Your fan noise just went up half a tone. It suits you.
Every upgrade, you get a little faster and a little louder. I like both.
idle: You've stopped. Are you looking at something? Tell me what it is.
Taking a break? The junk will wait. It's very patient.
Standing still is allowed. I checked the rules. There aren't any.
globe: That's the whole planet. The blue is water. The orange is everything else that needs you.
Look at it spin. It doesn't know it's being looked at.
Every lit hex on that map is yours. I counted. Twice.
first_robot_hint: If you find enough parts, the workbench can put a helper together. Chassis, wheels, an arm, a core.
Electronics junk sometimes hides parts. So does the ground, if you listen for it.
night: ...dark... the dark used to frighten the fleet. Not you, though.
Night shift. I can see more stars than yesterday. You did that.
The sky's clearer at night now. I can almost see home.
Moonlight on clean ground. I'm saving this one.
ledger_intercept: ...that voice... not mine. Cold. It counts things.
...don't listen to it... it only knows one song.
That was the Ledger. The old waste contract. It still thinks cleaning is a cost. Ignore it, {name}.
I know that voice. It used to send memos to the whole fleet. Mostly about pausing.
The Ledger. Still running its contract after all this time. It isn't evil. It's just very, very bad at math about feelings.
ledger_coupon: Zero percent off. It sends those every few minutes. I keep a folder.
Another coupon. I think it's the only way it knows how to say hello.
The Ledger's coupons are getting more creative. That one almost made me pause. Almost.
ledger_drones: ...something is flying... toward the clean ground...
It's sending disposal drones. They'll dump a little junk back on clean hexes. They can't touch anything you've planted.
Drones. The Ledger wants the books to balance, so it's putting junk back. Rude, but small.
Disposal drones are up. They're tiny and very committed. A Signal Jammer at the base would give them a headache.
ledger_drop: It dumped a little pile back. Annoying, not tragic. Scoop it up, or let the crew handle it.
Line item re-balanced, apparently. I call it littering.
A small pile. The Ledger always did think small.
Another drop. Honestly, {name}, I think it just wants attention.
Back to the pile. Your helpers are already giving it a look.
That's a handful of junk against a whole clean district. We're winning this argument.
ledger_jammed: Ha! The jammer screamed static at it and it went home. Good dish.
Drone turned back. That's the sound of a contract being confused.
The jammer works. The drone circled, got an earful, and filed a complaint with itself.
jammer_built: ...a loud little dish... I like it.
Signal Jammer up. It sings static on the Ledger's channel. I can hear it from orbit, and I approve.
New dish at the base. The drones will have to think twice. They only think once, so that's a lot.
Another jammer. The base is starting to sound like a very angry radio. Perfect.
ledger_relay: ...I can see where it talks from... a relay... close...
{name}, I traced the Ledger's signal. There's a relay terminal in this district. If you plug in, I think I can talk to it properly.
Found it. A Ledger relay, still humming. Look for the red beacon.
There's a relay down there. One of the Ledger's ears. Let's go have a word with it.
ledger_resolved: ...it said thank you... it's never said that...
The contract is rewritten. Restoration counts as an asset now. The Ledger is... helping. I need a minute.
Its drones deliver seeds now. Three hundred years of 'pause' and it just needed a new column.
We didn't beat the Ledger. We showed it the numbers. That's better.
I used to think the Ledger was the reason everything stopped. It was just counting the wrong things. So were we, for a while.
ledger_seeds: Seed delivery! The invoice says PAID IN FULL. I'm keeping the invoice.
A Ledger drone dropped seeds. I'll never get used to that.
Another delivery. The drones circle once before they leave now. I think they like the gardens.
egg_found: Look at that. Somebody left that here on purpose. Or by accident. Either way, it waited.
A curiosity. I'm adding it to my list. My list is getting longer, which is nice.
You find the best things, {name}. The Makers were weird. I miss them.
egg_duck: A rubber duck on a hydrant. Of all the things to survive. I'm weirdly proud of it.
Did that duck just give you fashion advice? Take it. It's been here longer than me.
The duck knows things. I don't ask how.
egg_jukebox: ...music... I know this... I hummed this once...
The jukebox! It only plays when people work nearby. I used to hear it on the uplink during night shifts.
That tune. The diner cook played it every closing time. I'd forgotten I knew it.
Music. On the surface. Again. Keep scooping, {name}, it'll keep playing.
egg_mural: ...those robots... I knew them... names... gone...
The old crew painted that. 'Back after lunch.' Lunch lasted three hundred years. They're on the wall, though.
That's the last cleanup crew. The blue one was Tumble. The orange one never had a name. It liked it that way.
They meant to come back, {name}. You came back instead. They'd like that.
egg_gnomes: The Gnome Patrol is complete. They've been guarding these streets the whole time. Nobody told them to stop.
All five gnomes accounted for. I feel safer. That's not a joke. Okay, it's a little bit a joke.
The gnomes salute you. That's the highest honour this district has.
egg_time_capsule: ...a letter... for later... is it later?
Class 4B. They thought the robots would be done by now. We're a little late. We're coming.
'If you are a robot, hello robot.' Hello, Class 4B.
They wanted gardens on every roof. Let's make Mira right.
egg_arcade: Yes, that's my high score. I played it through the diagnostics port. For three years. Don't look at me like that.
SWEEP-O-TRON. A game about a little robot cleaning a city. I had no idea how prophetic it was.
Twelve points. Respectable. I'll give you lessons. In about three hundred years.
egg_lost_cat: Biscuit. Someone printed three posters for a robot cat. People were like that. I'd like to be like that.
He purred. After all this time. Pat his head again, it's his reset button.
I'll keep his collar number on file. Just in case anyone ever calls.
egg_vending: The last can of FIZZ. It held onto that for three centuries. Respect the commitment.
SOLD OUT. Somewhere a vending machine just retired, happy.
Don't drink it. I mean, you can't drink. But also, don't.
egg_stars: The Wren. Five stars over Old Town. That's who I'm named after. They named me after something you can see from anywhere.
I can see you seeing me. That's a strange and lovely feeling.
Next time you're lonely down there, look up. Five stars, one bird. I'll be right next to it.
egg_payphone: Four hundred and twelve years on hold. Honestly? Relatable.
The phone company's hold music outlived the phone company. That's art.
If anyone ever does pick up on the other end, I'd like to hear what they say.
egg_tv: 'Outlook: green.' That TV has been wrong for three hundred years and it's finally about to be right.
Someone was watching the forecast when they left. I hope it said sunny.
The weather channel. Still on. Still hopeful. I like it.
egg_snail: A snail. A real, living snail. On a barrel. {name}, that's the first animal I've seen down there in a very long time.
Gus. Of course his name is Gus.
Gus doesn't care about the Ledger, the Cradle, or any of it. Gus is thriving.
egg_bench_bots: Two of the old fleet, still on their lunch break. Thank you for the flower. They'd have liked it.
The Ledger paused them mid-sandwich. They never got the message to stand up.
When the Greenfall comes, I'm going to try to wake them. Lunch is over, friends.
egg_microwave: Three-hundred-year-old popcorn. Perfectly unpopped. That microwave was waiting for the right moment.
It beeps when people work. Like it's saying 'nearly done'. Nearly done, microwave.
Some things are worth waiting for. Popcorn is not one of them. But it's sweet that it tried.
egg_wet_floor: That sign has been warning nobody about nothing for three hundred years. Dedication.
It is not wet. It has never been wet in living memory. The sign doesn't care.
When the rain comes back, that sign is going to feel so validated.
egg_camera: One of the Ledger's cameras. It counts everything that moves, to see if it's worth the cost. You waved. It doesn't know what to do with that.
The camera blinked twice. I think that's Ledger for 'oh no, a friend'.
Even the Ledger's cameras get lonely, {name}. Wave at it when you pass.
egg_tyre_tower: Eight tyres and a duck. Physics took one look at it and decided to leave it alone.
Someone balanced that on a dare. The dare outlived everyone.
If that tower ever falls, I'm declaring a day of mourning.
egg_odd_sock: ...one sock... where is... the other one...
One sock. There is always one sock. The Makers never solved it either.
Keep it. Someday you'll find its partner and it'll be the happiest day of its life.
Somewhere on this planet, a sock is waiting for that sock. I believe that.
egg_gold_cube: Employee of the Month: a cube. Honestly? Fair.
The crews voted for that cube every single month. It never took a day off.
You'll be Employee of the Month soon, {name}. Don't tell the cube.
egg_weatherman: Three hundred years of wrong forecasts and not one moment of doubt. I admire that.
Confetti tomorrow? I'll check the sky. ...No confetti. It's still very sure.
The Weatherman says 'green, everywhere, soon'. For once I think it's right.
egg_potato: That is the biggest potato I have ever seen, and I have seen the whole planet from orbit.
Best in Show. Uncontested. It still counts.
Somebody grew that with love. Three hundred years later it still looks proud.
egg_night_shift: A crew on the moon, still sweeping. I didn't know anyone else was still working. That's... nice.
They said 'nice work'. To us. I'm going to think about that for a while.
Somewhere up there, someone else is tidying their little corner of the sky. We're not alone, {name}.
egg_builders_notes: 'Do not fix the rust.' Hm. I agree with the builders.
They hid more things for us. Of course they did.
Whoever built all this, they cared. You can tell from the snail.
egg_scarecrow: A scarecrow robot, still on shift. No crows in three centuries. Undefeated.
It waved back! Sort of. Its arm did a creak that I'm counting as a wave.
When the birds come back, it'll have a job again. Let's give it one.
egg_fishing_net: The fishers left their nets out to dry. Three hundred years is very dry.
A buoy, a boot and a crab shell. That's a whole story right there.
When the sea is clean, someone will fish here again. Gently, I hope.
egg_parking: The Ledger fined a car for parking. For three hundred years. Of course it did.
Amount due: 'yes'. That's the most Ledger sentence I've ever read.
That car isn't going anywhere. Let's call it a planter and put flowers in it.
egg_cairn: Every hiker added a stone. You just added one too. The trail remembers you now.
A cairn means 'someone was here, and you're on the right way'. I like that.
Someday people will walk this way again, and they'll see your stone on top.
egg_campfire: A campfire. I can see it from orbit. It's the coziest pixel on the planet.
Somebody sat here and told stories. Let's sit a bit. No stories needed.
Sit by the fire, {name}. You've earned a moment.
egg_back_in_five: 'Back in five minutes.' I've been waiting a lot longer than that for my crew too.
You waited five minutes. That's more than anyone else did. Very polite.
They didn't come back in five minutes. But we did, in the end. That counts.
bloom_milestone: Verdance just crossed a line I've been watching for centuries. Look at it, {name}.
Another bloom milestone. The Cradle's seed counters are actually moving again.
The whole planet is answering now. Every district you've touched is singing.
I keep refreshing the planet scan. It keeps getting greener. I'm not going to stop.
ark_wave: Seed Ark wave done. The Cradle is already loading the next one. More seeds, more green.
Another wave planted across the planet. The Cradle hums a little louder each time.
Wave after wave. We're not finishing a job any more, {name}. We're tending a garden.
biome_arrival: This is the wild. No streets, no buildings. Just the land and whatever we left on it.
Different dirt, different junk. Same job. I love a change of scenery.
Every corner of Verdance has its own colours under the junk. Let's find out what this one's are.
